declarations.description:
Tab strip that shows one content panel at a time.

Light-DOM children are split in two groups: every `<c2-tab for="…">` becomes a tab in the header,
every other child is a panel whose `id` matches a tab's `for`. Only the panel of the selected tab is
shown. The header is a `tablist`: Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs, Enter and Space
activate the focused one.

The strip assigns its children to its slots itself (manual slot assignment), so neither the tabs nor the
panels need a `slot` attribute and none is written on them; a `slot="tab"` already in the markup is
harmless. Each panel sits in a wrapper of the shadow root; the shown one carries `role="tabpanel"` and is
labelled by its tab, and the others are `hidden="until-found"`: the browser's find-in-page (and a
text-fragment link) still finds the text of every enabled tab and selects that tab, firing
`selection-change` as a click does. Where `until-found` is unsupported the other panels are simply hidden.
A panel that carries its own `role` keeps it and the wrapper adds none. Without element reflection
(`ariaLabelledByElements`), the selected panel gets `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby` itself (and the
tab an `id` for it), unless the author wrote them.

A strip with more tabs than room (six tabs on a phone) sets `overflow="scroll"`: the tab list scrolls sideways, the
selected tab is scrolled into view whenever it changes, the arrow keys reach every tab, and an edge fades out on a
side where tabs are hidden (`--c2-tabs__fade--width`), as in `c2-tab-nav`. The scrollbar is hidden unless `--c2-tabs--scrollbar-width`
says otherwise.

Strips that share a `sync-key` move together: picking a tab in one selects the tab with the same label in every
other strip of the page with that key (a package manager, a language), and the choice is remembered in
`localStorage` and restored when the page loads again. That is how a set of code blocks keeps one switcher.

When the shadow root was server-rendered (declarative shadow DOM, which has no manual mode) the strip falls
back to writing `slot` on the tabs and the selected panel, and only that panel is rendered. The selected tab
matches `c2-tab:state(selected)`.
declarations.name: Tabs

slots.name: tab

slots.description: The panel of the selected tab, in a server-rendered shadow root only (assigned from the child whose `id` matches `selected-tab`). Otherwise each panel is assigned to a wrapper of its own; no `slot` attribute is needed either way.

members.name: ariaLabel
members.description: Accessible name for the tab list.

members.name: selectedTab
members.description: `for` value of the selected tab (and `id` of the visible panel). Falls back to the first enabled tab.

members.name: syncKey
members.description:
Name of a group of strips that switch together. Picking a tab selects the tab with the same label (its `label`,
else its `aria-label`, else its text) in every strip of the page with this key, and the label is remembered in
`localStorage` under `c2n-tabs:<sync-key>`, so the strip opens on it on the next visit. A strip that has no tab with
that label keeps its own. A remembered choice is applied once the tabs are slotted, in place of `selected-tab`.

members.name: overflow
members.description:
What happens when the tabs are wider than the strip. `visible` (default): they run past its edge. `scroll`: the
tab list scrolls sideways, keeps the selected tab in view and fades the edges where tabs are hidden.

members.name: restored
members.description: Whether the remembered `sync-key` choice has been looked up.

members.name: measured
members.description:
False until the indicator has been placed once: the first placement must not animate. The indicator is placed by
writing its style directly, not through reactive state: it is measured in `updated`, and a state change there
would schedule a second render for every selection.

members.name: panels
members.description: Panels, one wrapper each (manual slot assignment only; a server-rendered root uses the `tab-content` slot).

members.name: childObserver
members.description: Tabs and panels added or removed later are (re)assigned to their slots.

members.name: manualSlots
members.description:
Whether this strip assigns its slots by hand. False only when the shadow root came from declarative shadow DOM
(server rendering), which is always in named mode; the strip then falls back to `slot` attributes.

members.name: assignSlots
members.description: Puts every `<c2-tab>` child in the `tab` slot, then re-resolves the visible panel.

members.name: tabs
members.description: Slotted `<c2-tab>` elements, in DOM order.

members.name: select
members.description: Selects a tab and notifies listeners. Ignores unknown or disabled tabs.

members.name: pick
members.description: Selects a tab and fires `selection-change`; returns the tab when the selection changed.

members.name: handleSync
members.description: Another strip of the page picked a tab: follow it when it is in this strip's group and this strip has that label.

members.name: restoreSync
members.description: Selects the tab of the choice its `sync-key` group remembers, once, silently.

members.name: syncTabs
members.description: Mirrors `selectedTab` onto the tabs (selected state, roving tabindex) and the panels (slot, ARIA).

members.name: collectPanels
members.description:
Updates `panels` (the children named by a tab, each rendered in a wrapper of its own) when the set changed. Called
from `willUpdate` so a render already has them, and from the child observer between renders.

members.name: syncPanels
members.description: Shows the panel of the selected tab and gives the panels the `tabpanel` semantics they lack.

members.name: handleBeforeMatch
members.description:
Find-in-page matched text in a hidden panel: select its tab the way a click does, through a cancelable
`tab-change`. A vetoed switch hides the panel again once the browser has revealed it.

members.name: revealSelected
members.description:
Scrolls a scrolling strip so the selected tab is wholly in view, `--c2-tabs__fade--width` (the scroll padding) away
from either edge. Only the tab list moves: unlike `scrollIntoView`, the page never scrolls.

members.name: updateScrollEdges
members.description:
Marks the edges of a scrolling strip behind which tabs are hidden, for the fades. Classes on the strip inside the
shadow root, written directly: this runs on every scroll frame and must not schedule a render.

events.name: selection-change
events.description: Fired after the user selects another tab, including when this strip follows a pick made in another strip of its `sync-key` group. `detail.value` is the new `selected-tab`. Not fired for programmatic changes, nor when a remembered choice is restored. Does not bubble: several components fire `selection-change`, so a listener belongs on the element itself rather than on an ancestor. The name matches `c2-list`, `c2-select` and `c2-table`; it is deliberately not `change`, which every native form control bubbles — a `c2-text-field` inside a panel would otherwise reach a listener meant for the tab strip.

declarations.description:
A single tab inside `<c2-tabs>`. Its `for` attribute names the `id` of the panel it controls.
The parent owns selection: it sets `selected` and the roving `tabindex`; this element exposes
them as `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` and `aria-disabled` through `ElementInternals`, so no host attribute is written.
The selected tab matches `c2-tab:state(selected)`.

Given an `href`, the tab is a link instead, for `<c2-tab-nav>`: it renders an `<a>` that covers the whole tab, is
a `listitem` rather than a `tab`, and `current` marks it as the page being shown (`aria-current="page"`). A link tab
belongs in `<c2-tab-nav>` only: inside `<c2-tabs>` it is not supported, and `for` and `disabled` do not apply to it.
declarations.name: Tab

cssParts.description: The `<a>` of a tab that has an `href`. It wraps the label and covers the tab.
cssParts.name: link

Set by the parent `<c2-tabs>`; do not set by hand. Not reflected: the strip selects a tab while the page upgrades,

declarations.description:
A row of tabs that are links, for navigation between pages: a repository's Code / Issues / Settings, the sections
of an account. It has the look of `<c2-tabs>` but not its behaviour: there are no panels and no selection; each
`<c2-tab href="…">` is a link the user follows, and the one marked `current` is the page being shown.

It is a navigation landmark (name it with `aria-label`) holding a list of links, the `current` one announced as
`aria-current="page"`. Every link is a Tab stop of its own; there are no arrow keys, which belong to a `tablist`.
The current tab's indicator is its bottom border, drawn with CSS, so a server-rendered strip shows it before any
script runs. When the tabs do not fit, the strip scrolls sideways with its scrollbar hidden; an edge with more tabs
beyond it fades out, and the current tab is scrolled into view.

Mark the current tab where the page is rendered (`<c2-tab href="/issues" current>`), or move `current` from the
application's router. The strip sets nothing on its tabs.
declarations.name: TabNav

cssProperties.description: Space between an icon and the label inside a tab.

cssParts.description: The scrolling row wrapping the default slot of links; it draws the strip's line and does not style inside the assigned tabs.
cssParts.name: list

members.name: edges
members.description: Reports whether the first and the last tab are fully in view, to fade the edges that are not.

members.name: tabs
members.description: The `<c2-tab>` links, in DOM order.

members.name: currentObserver
members.description: Brings the moved tab into view when the application moves `current` (a router), which fires no `slotchange`.

members.name: revealCurrent
members.description:
Scrolls the strip, and only the strip, so the current tab is in view. Not `scrollIntoView`: without its `container`
option (Newly available) it would scroll the page too.
